findings.sourceEvidence: "provided that the amount of charges or nonrecurring merger costs incurred during such period as a result of any such transaction that is not successful or consummated shall not exceed $5,000,000 in the aggregate"
findings.proposedIrEvidence: operand exprId ir-expr:8133c9562902acd84635bde7 quotes the $5,000,000 language verbatim in sourceEvidence but is typed as kind="UNSUPPORTED" with no numeric AMOUNT node anywhere in the IR representing the cap; the deterministic pass independently confirms the literal value 5000000 never appears as a typed AMOUNT anywhere in the compiled IR
findings.verifierReasoning: Unlike the other exclusion items in this definition, which genuinely require qualitative GAAP judgment (impairments, mark-to-market, accounting policy changes, etc.), the $5,000,000 aggregate cap on charges/nonrecurring merger costs for unsuccessful or non-consummated transactions is a plain, unambiguous, extractable numeric threshold stated in dollars with no GAAP judgment required to identify its value. Bundling this literal figure into a category-wide UNSUPPORTED node with the same 'qualitative GAAP-determined adjustment' style reasoning used for genuinely qualitative items risks losing a concrete, independently trackable numeric constraint that a downstream basket/definition-tracking process would reasonably expect to find as a structured value. A hypothetical transaction incurring $6,000,000 of abandoned-deal costs would need this cap to correctly compute Consolidated Net Income, and nothing in the IR's structure currently exposes that ceiling for automated or semi-automated verification, even though the raw text was captured. I flag this as uncertain rather than clearly material because the entire calculationExpression is already marked UNSUPPORTED/requiredReview and sufficiency is honestly PARTIAL (not COMPLETE), which substantially mitigates the risk that a consumer would silently over-rely on this node.'
